lba_qa.q: A triangular park has sides 13 m, 14 m and 15 m. Find its area using Heron's formula.
lba_qa.a:
Heron's formula: Area = square root of [s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)]
where s = (a + b + c)/2

Given a = 13, b = 14, c = 15.

Step 1 - Find s:
s = (13 + 14 + 15)/2 = 42/2 = 21 m

Step 2 - Apply formula:
Area = square root of [21 x (21-13) x (21-14) x (21-15)]
= square root of [21 x 8 x 7 x 6]
= square root of 7056
= 84 square metres ✅

lba_qa.q: A triangular signboard has all three sides equal to 6 cm (equilateral). Find s (the semi-perimeter) and set up Heron's formula.
lba_qa.a:
For an equilateral triangle, all sides = 6 cm.

Step 1 - Semi-perimeter s:
s = (6 + 6 + 6)/2 = 18/2 = 9 cm ✅

Step 2 - Heron's formula setup:
Area = square root of [s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)]
= square root of [9 x (9-6) x (9-6) x (9-6)]
= square root of [9 x 3 x 3 x 3]
= square root of 243
= about 15.6 square cm ✅

lba_qa.q: A triangular plot has sides 5 m, 12 m and 13 m. Find its area using Heron's formula.
lba_qa.a:
Heron's formula: Area = square root of [s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)]

Given a = 5, b = 12, c = 13.

Step 1 - Semi-perimeter:
s = (5 + 12 + 13)/2 = 30/2 = 15 m

Step 2 - Apply:
Area = square root of [15 x (15-5) x (15-12) x (15-13)]
= square root of [15 x 10 x 3 x 2]
= square root of 900
= 30 square metres ✅

lba_qa.q: A gardener has a triangular flower bed with sides 8 m, 8 m and 4 m. Find its semi-perimeter s.
lba_qa.a:
Semi-perimeter s = (sum of all three sides)/2

Given sides: 8 m, 8 m, 4 m.

s = (8 + 8 + 4)/2
= 20/2
= 10 m ✅

So the semi-perimeter is 10 m. (This value is then used in Heron's formula to find the area.)

lba_qa.q: Why is Heron's formula especially useful for finding the area of a triangular field when you only have the three side lengths?
lba_qa.a:
Heron's formula needs ONLY the three sides — no height required.

Usefulness:
- The usual area formula (1/2 x base x height) needs the HEIGHT
- In a real field, measuring the perpendicular height is often hard
- But the three sides can be measured easily with a tape ✅
- Heron's formula uses just those sides: Area = square root of [s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)]

So it is ideal for irregular triangular plots where only sides are known.

lba_qa.q: A triangular tile has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Find its area using Heron's formula and verify it is a right triangle.
lba_qa.a:
Step 1 - Semi-perimeter:
s = (3 + 4 + 5)/2 = 12/2 = 6 cm

Step 2 - Heron's formula:
Area = square root of [6 x (6-3) x (6-4) x (6-5)]
= square root of [6 x 3 x 2 x 1]
= square root of 36
= 6 square cm ✅

Verify right triangle: 3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5^2. Yes, it is right-angled. (Check: (1/2)(3)(4) = 6, matches.)

lba_qa.q: A triangular banner has sides 9 m, 12 m and 15 m. Find its semi-perimeter and the value of (s - a) for the side a = 9 m.
lba_qa.a:
Step 1 - Semi-perimeter:
s = (9 + 12 + 15)/2 = 36/2 = 18 m

Step 2 - Find (s - a) for a = 9:
= 18 - 9
= 9 m ✅

So s = 18 m and (s - 9) = 9 m. These are then put into Heron's formula along with (s - 12) and (s - 15) to get the area.
